Tools are available in this conversation. Their signatures are listed within <tools> </tools> XML tags. Use a tool only when the request needs it; otherwise just answer in natural language. Don't make assumptions about values to plug into functions. After a call you will receive its result within <tool_response> </tool_response> XML tags.
Here are the available tools:
<tools>
{"name": "get_weather", "description": "Get weather <city>", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}, "unit": {"type": "string", "enum": ["c", "f"]}}, "required": ["city"]}}
{"name": "mem0_search", "description": "Search memories", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}}}}
</tools>
To call a tool, write EXACTLY one or more blocks of the form:
<tool_call>
{"name": "<function-name>", "arguments": {...}}
</tool_call>
Rules: the JSON inside <tool_call> MUST use double quotes and be valid JSON. Output NOTHING else on the lines of a <tool_call> block. If you are not calling a tool, never emit <tool_call>. Write the block as plain text inside your normal reply; this text block is the only way to call these tools.
